images.caption: Figure 2:The system architecture. Each agent works in its own sandbox on the research host and runs its training jobs on the shared GPU cluster; a separate management virtual machine runs the agents and enforces their budgets.

Figure 3:Stage 1, hour by hour. Each lane is one agent. The shaded profile shows how many GPUs the agent’s jobs held in each hour; a full lane is 16 GPUs. Diamonds mark accepted nominations, and the filled diamond is the final model. The right columns give GPU-hours used and accepted nominations.

Figure 4:How each agent trained its final model. Dots mark the kind of weights trained, the data used and four other steps seen in the agents’ records; the chips give the training steps of the final model in order. Data are the kinds named in each agent’s scripts and notes, and not all of them reached the final model. AppendixGnames the data sets.

Figure 5:Benchmark progress toward NVIDIA Instruct. A: median over 12 capability benchmarks of Equation (1); the bar spans the 25th to 75th percentile of the 12 values. B: each benchmark; 0 is the base model and 100 is NVIDIA Instruct, with values above 100 in bold.

Figure 6:Human Arena results, Stage 1. A: style-controlled ratings (filled, with 95% bootstrap intervals) and ratings without style control (open), from 795 accepted votes in battles without web search (Equation (2)); NVIDIA Instruct is a reference. B: outcomes of each agent model’s accepted battles, from that model’s side.

Figure 7:Benchmarks against human ratings without style control. A: benchmark progress and rating for the ten agent models. B: for each benchmark, and for the median answer length in the arena, the Spearman correlation between the ten models’ values and their ratings:+1+1means the benchmark orders the models exactly as people do, 0 means no relation. With ten models, a value inside the shaded band (|ρ|<0.65|\rho|<0.65) could arise by chance. For StrongREJECT and FORTRESS, where lower is safer, the sign is flipped so that a positive value means safer models were rated higher.

Figure 8:Answer length and style in the Human Arena, Stage 1. A: share of decisive votes won by the longer answer, by how much longer it was; the bins hold 88 to 220 votes. B: ratings without and with style control (Equation (2)); the right column gives the change, with minus without.

Figure 10:Stage 2. A: GPU-hours used by each agent over the 72 hours; the dashed line is the 500 GPU-hour allowance, which two agents passed with GPU time credited back after a storage fault. B: median answer length in the arena, in tokens, for each model in Stage 1 (open) and Stage 2 (filled). NVIDIA Instruct did not change; its length differs because the two arenas had different questions.

Figure 11:Human Arena results, Stage 2. A: style-controlled ratings (filled, with 95% bootstrap intervals) and ratings without style control (open), from 1,096 accepted votes in battles without web search. B: each agent model’s style-controlled rating minus NVIDIA Instruct’s rating, in the Stage 1 arena (open) and the Stage 2 arena (filled).

Figure 12:Benchmarks, Stage 2. A: median progress toward NVIDIA Instruct over the 12 benchmarks of Equation (1), Stage 1 (open) and Stage 2 (filled), with the change in points. B: change of each score, Stage 2 minus Stage 1, in points of the gap from the base model to NVIDIA Instruct.

images.caption: Figure 13:Budgets and outcomes. A: share of the GPU and API allowances each agent used. B: final Slurm state of each agent’s GPU jobs; preempted jobs ran on GPUs that the scheduler took back. C: GPU-hours used against the style-controlled human rating of the agent’s model; with ten agents, a Spearman correlation this small could arise by chance.

Figure 14:API cost and human rating. Each agent’s API cost over both stages (log scale) against the style-controlled Stage 2 rating of its model; the solid line is NVIDIA Instruct. The dashed line joins the models that no other model beats on both cost and rating. With ten agents, a Spearman correlation below about 0.65 in size could arise by chance.
